question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

The captain said, "We have been sailing in these choppy waters for two days, and we expect that the storm, which is now on the horizon, will hit us in a few hours."

options.text: The captain said that they have been sailing in these choppy waters for two days, and they expect that the storm, which is now on the horizon, will hit them in a few hours.
The captain said that they had been sailing in those choppy waters for two days, and they expected that the storm, which was then on the horizon, would hit them in a few hours.
The captain said that they had been sailing in these choppy waters for two days, and they expected that the storm, which was then on the horizon, would hit them in a few hours.
The captain said that they had been sailing in those choppy waters for two days, and they expected that the storm, which is now on the horizon, will hit them in a few hours.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Indirect Speech:** The captain said that they had been sailing in those choppy waters for two days, and they expected that the storm, which was then on the horizon, would hit them in a few hours.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Changes:**
 
 
• "We" becomes "they" to match the third person in reported speech.
 
• "these" becomes "those" to reflect the change in perspective.
 
 
 
• **Tense Changes:**
 
 
• Present perfect "have been sailing" changes to past perfect &
